messages:
Aria: quick Q 3 partner onboarding: should we permit a single API key to be used by multiple projects for partners? it's convenient but messy for billing/quotas. thoughts?

Tom: i'd avoid multi-project keys by default. two pragmatic options we've used:
- project-bound keys (created with an explicit project id list)
- an exchange flow: partner keeps a master onboarding key; they call our API to mint short-lived project tokens.

Sofia: +1 on exchange. project-bound keys make telemetry and billing straightforward. if we add exchange, we need to persist provenance (who minted what for which project) and reflect that in billing dashboards.

Aria: about legacy keys currently reused across teams: could we offer an exchange shim that accepts legacy_key + target_project and returns a scoped token? rollout it behind a flag to limit initial exposure.

Tom: console UX needs to be explicit. when creating an org- or partner-scoped key show a modal: "Billing responsibility" with a required selection of billing project and an optional checkbox "allow usage by other projects (explicit acceptance required)". also include a later action to restrict scope.

Sofia: telemetry notes 4 emit per-request headers: `x-rw-origin: project:<id>`, `x-rw-service: svc:<id>`, `x-rw-key: <key_id>`. avoid using raw ids as high-cardinality tags in long-term metrics; instead derive low-cardinality rollups like `billing_project`, `key_scope` (project/org/partner). trace/endpoint sampling should keep ids for debug.

Aria: agree on rollups. sampling policy: full traces for errors and billing changes; 0.2% for normal requests. also add an alert for `unattributed_request_count` when > threshold.

Tom: security: exchange endpoint must validate that requester is allowed to request tokens for the target project. require `consent_signature` from the project owner for cross-owner mints, and log every mint to audit.

Sofia: rollout plan proposal:
phase A: collect telemetry only (accept new headers but don't enforce). add `effective_billing_project` to billing UI.
phase B: opt-in enforcement for selected orgs / partners.
phase C: enforce by default for new keys and provide migration tooling for legacy keys.

Aria: implementation idea: middleware decides the `billing_project` and populates a request-level auth context. it should also consult an allowlist for org-admin approved cross-project keys.

Tom: migration tools: list legacy keys with live traffic, offer console wizard to convert them to per-project scoped tokens, show expected billing delta pre/post. for high-volume partners provide a bulk exchange endpoint.

Sofia: ops: add rate-limits and an SLO for the exchange endpoint (p95 < 150ms). also limit exchange attempts per legacy key to avoid abuse.

Aria: proto draft for exchange API:```
POST /v1/keys/exchange
Auth: Bearer <onboarding_key>
Body: { "target_project": "proj:alpha", "ttl_seconds": 3600, "consent_signature": "<signed>" }
Response: { "access_token": "tok_...", "expires_at": "2026-11-01T12:00:00Z", "billing_project": "proj:alpha" }
```

Tom: require `consent_signature` when target_project != owner(onboarding_key). console will provide a one-click signer to generate the signature.

Sofia: storage detail: write an immutable `key_mint_event` record for each exchange with fields: issuer_key, minted_token_id, target_project, consent_present. helpful for audits/postmortems.

infra-bot: created issue INFRA-6721: "partner-key exchange + billing attribution" labels: auth, telemetry, console, migration

Aria: great. next actions: Tom to spec middleware and rate-limits; Sofia to add billing column + telemetry alert; I'll mock the console modal and migration wizard. i'll link the mock in #design later.

Tom: added to next eng sync agenda.

Sofia: i'll draft the migration email and an FAQ for partners.
